paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me. God takes it seriously when His people walk away from Him. The LORD says the land is "flagrantly prostituting itself by departing from the LORD" (Hosea 1:2). Hosea's home, his marriage and his kids' names all carry that message.

Now hear this, because it matters for you and me. Those three names get heavier each time, and the last one is the hardest: "you are not My people, and I am not your God" (Hosea 1:9). I think that one hurts, and I think it's supposed to. When God warns, He means it, and we shouldn't shrug it off or wait around hoping it just goes away.

But look at what else is sitting right in the middle of this. God says, "I will have compassion on the house of Judah, and I will save them," and He says it will be "not by bow or sword or war, not by horses and cavalry, but by the LORD their God" (Hosea 1:7). So the rescue never comes from our own strength. It comes from Him. Hang on to that, baker, because Hosea's story isn't over.
